# Portfolio Discipline

Investing decisions need a written thesis, position sizing, risk limits, and a review cadence. A portfolio can survive normal volatility when each allocation has a reason, a maximum loss, and a trigger for reassessment. Markets punish vague conviction. Before adding to a position, check whether the original facts improved or whether the trade is only averaging down because the price moved against you.

Long term investment work is mostly process: keep a watchlist, separate macro signals from company fundamentals, rebalance when concentration becomes accidental, and document why cash, bonds, index funds, or individual equities belong in the same portfolio.
